I will keep things simple and steady this year. In Quzhou County, the safest way for me is still the usual wheat-maize cycle, because the land, water, machinery, and my own habits all match it. I am 71, so I do not want to spread myself across too many crops or take on work that is too fine or risky. I will use improved or hybrid seed, put fertilizer in at moderate levels, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and control pests only a few times when pressure shows up. For wheat, I will focus on good base fertilizer, one sowing after land preparation, and a few key irrigations around wintering, jointing, and grain filling if water allows. After wheat harvest, I will quickly plant summer maize, use hybrid seed for stable ears and yield, give nitrogen in split applications, and keep the field clean and simple to manage. I will stay with rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing and fits my workload.
